title: check.py's code citation scan reads each tool file without walking every node of its syntax tree
goal: check.code_citation_errors finds the same citation errors, so test_check_programs.py's code citation test still passes, and on the live tree takes at most 0.3 s, best of three in one process

run: import sys,time;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import check;t=[];[(t.append(time.perf_counter()),check.code_citation_errors(),t.append(time.perf_counter())) for _ in range(3)];b=min(t[i+1]-t[i] for i in range(0,6,2));print(round(b,3));sys.exit(0 if b<=0.3 else 1)

clauses.clause: check.code_citation_errors finds the same citation errors, so test_check_programs.py's code citation test still passes
on the live tree takes at most 0.3 s, best of three in one process

notes: Premise, measured 2026-10-14 on a quiet darwin host: check.py on the live tree takes 1.32 s, and code_citation_errors 0.78 to 0.80 s of it (best of three in one process); profiled, code_citation_errors is 1.73 of 2.30 s, almost all in code_comment_lines: ast.parse plus ast.walk over all 90 _tools/*.py files (609 237 walk calls) and tokenize, to find docstring and comment lines. check.py runs 12 times in a whole-suite run (7 in test_sync_e2e.py's and test_prepush_e2e.py's gate runs, 14.1 s summed), and once in every real sync gate. A docstring is the first statement of a module, class or def body, so the scan needs no walk of expression nodes; a file whose text holds no kb/ citation needs no parse.
